text:
sarah-pm: quick heads-up — customer X just pushed back on our quotas PRD. They need per-route billing/limits and deterministic pricing exposure for their legal team. can we sync on scope?
ajay-eng: thanks — do they mean per-endpoint (e.g. /v1/chat vs /v1/embeddings) or per-application route (custom routes)?
mar ia-data: they called out both. main ask: show cost/limits at route level in the console and on invoices. wants predictable unit price for each route.
kim-plat: that affects metering and the limits API. current model meters tokens + embeddings globally per tenant. per-route would need tagging at ingest and separate counters. rough rollback: tagging costs + storage for counters.
zane-sre: operationally we also need to decide fallbacks. if a route hits quota, do we: 1) 429 only for that route, 2) failover to a cheaper model, or 3) queue/buffer until capacity frees? we should spell acceptance criteria.
sarah-pm: acceptance criteria proposal: 
- UI: route-level limits UI to create a limit with name, unit (tokens/requests/embeddings), window, and price override.
- API: PATCH /v1/tenants/{id}/limits routes: [{route_id, unit, limit, price_override_cents}] and GET to show current consumption.
- Billing: invoices must break out charges by route; no changes to existing tenant-level billing for customers who opt out.
- Behavior: when a route limit is reached, return 429 for that route. optional auto-fallback to compatible route only if customer enables policy.
ajay-eng: +1 on explicit 429 default. technical note: per-route counters add cardinality risks — customers with many dynamic routes could blow up DB. suggest enforcing route naming constraints and default aggregate bucketing (e.g., route prefix).
leo-eng: for metering, we can attach a small routing key to every request (route_id) and aggregate into a time-series store. If route count grows > 1000 we auto-aggregate per-prefix. implementation: lightweight in nginx/lb, then async publish to metering pipeline.
maria-data: analytics/invoice generation needs idempotent, ordered events. we must preserve event ordering for accurate per-route token counts. also add reconciliation job: compare +/– 1% vs sample.
kim-plat: UI/Console impacts: limits page needs nested rows (tenant -> route -> window). also new guardrails for editing active limits during rollout. need a migration path for existing limits -> new per-route defaults.
zane-sre: SLO risk: increased cardinality may impact query perf in our observability. add per-tenant rate-limits for telemetry ingestion.
sarah-pm: edge cases to call out in PRD:
- dynamic routes created by customers (e.g., per-customer keys)
- retroactive billing adjustments if we detect misattribution
- model fallback pricing difference when fallback enabled
- partial requests spanning multiple routes (proxy rewrite)
ajay-eng: propose RFC sections: data model, API shape, UI mocks, metering pipeline changes, rollback plan, and cost estimate. I'll draft data model.
leo-eng: sample API snippet for RFC: 
```
PATCH /v1/tenants/123/limits
{
  "routes": [
    {"route_id": "chat/default", "unit": "tokens", "limit": 2000000, "price_override_cents": 12},
    {"route_id": "embeddings/v1", "unit": "units", "limit": 100000, "price_override_cents": 20}
  ]
}
```

kim-plat: also add GET /v1/tenants/123/usage?window=1h&group_by=route for UI.
maria-data: for billing we should write pseudo-SQL in RFC that shows SUM(token_count * price_per_token) GROUP BY route and then roll into tenant invoice lines. include tolerance window for late events.
billing-bot: system: invoice generation job ran 02:15 UTC, 0 migrations pending.
sarah-pm: launch gating proposal:
- Beta: opt-in per-route limits for up to 50 tenants, must pass billing reconciliation tests (<=0.5% variance vs baseline) and UI smoke.
- GA: open to all tenants after 3 weeks of beta with no critical billing incidents.
- Rollout: gradual, region by region, with telemetry and throttles.
zane-sre: add canary: route-level limits enabled for internal account + 3 customers on each region for 48 hours. record incidents.
ajay-eng: risks & mitigation to include in RFC:
- misattribution of tokens -> reconciliation job and refund flow.
- cardinality blowup -> enforced naming policy + auto-aggregation.
- billing disputes -> easy export of raw events per invoice line.
sarah-pm: owners: Ajay (API & data model), Kim (console + UX), Maria (billing & reconciliation), Zane (SRE rollout and canary), Leo (metering pipeline). timeline: draft RFC by EOW, engineering spikes next sprint.
leo-eng: question — do we need to expose price_override on invoices or only used for billing calc? customers asked to see price per-route on invoice lines. prefer show both unit_price and effective_price.
maria-data: agree, invoice line fields: description, units, unit_price_cents, total_cents, route_id, metadata.
sarah-pm: next steps: Ajay posts RFC link here when ready. Kim to mock UI by Tue. Maria to run a small billing sim. Zane to schedule canary infra. 
ajay-eng: I'll start the RFC draft now. ping me if you want to be added to reviewers. :thumbsup:
kim-plat: ack — will do UI mocks and attach screenshots. :eyes:
sarah-pm: thanks all. keeping this thread as source-of-truth for scope decisions. follow-ups in RFC PR. :white_check_mark:
billing-bot: system: RFC created by ajay-eng: https://internal.redwood.ai/rfc/PR-4321
